core.title: Reference every DESIRED OUTCOME from at least one feature
core.given: The plan contains one or more DESIRED OUTCOMES.
core.when: You author, change or validate the plan.
core.then: Every DESIRED OUTCOME must appear in the declared DESIRED OUTCOME list of at least one feature (DESIRED OUTCOME -> feature coverage).
prefer: When authoring a DESIRED OUTCOME, add it in the same change to the declared DESIRED OUTCOME list of the feature it serves.
When splitting, renaming or removing a feature, re-home each of its DESIRED OUTCOMES into another feature's declared DESIRED OUTCOME list.
avoid: Orphan DESIRED OUTCOMES that no feature references, whether new or pre-existing.
Gaming coverage by dumping unrelated DESIRED OUTCOMES into an arbitrary or catch-all feature just to satisfy the check.
core.why: A DESIRED OUTCOME that no feature references is untraceable to user-facing value and falls outside capability/feature coverage; DESIRED OUTCOME -> feature coverage is the link that lets lower-level coverage (DESIRED OUTCOME -> acceptance) roll up to features and product capabilities.
evidence: The DESIRED OUTCOME -> feature coverage check passes: every DESIRED OUTCOME appears in at least one feature's declared DESIRED OUTCOME list.
A reviewer can map each DESIRED OUTCOME in the plan to a feature whose list names it.
verification: The check covers the DESIRED OUTCOME -> feature direction only: it requires every DESIRED OUTCOME to be named by at least one feature and does not check the feature -> DESIRED OUTCOME direction (a feature listing DESIRED OUTCOMES beyond the minimum is not a violation).
The check is whole-plan: it applies to every DESIRED OUTCOME in the plan, including orphans that pre-exist the current change, not only to newly changed files.

The check enumerates both sides of coverage by plan-artifact kind from the profile: the covered artifacts (DESIRED OUTCOMES) and the covering artifacts (features), the latter each carrying a coverage list read through the profile's coverage-list construct, and requires every covered DESIRED OUTCOME to be named by at least one covering feature; the concrete validator and finding identifiers of this rule are realization details named by each stack.
Disposition: documentation-only (per-rule severity and disposition are properties of the rule, not profile data).

fires: The plan contains a DESIRED OUTCOME that no feature's declared DESIRED OUTCOME list names, including orphans that pre-exist the current change.
The plan contains DESIRED OUTCOMES but no features at all.
A feature exists but declares no DESIRED OUTCOME list, leaving DESIRED OUTCOMES unreferenced.

Example changes that commonly create orphans: adding a DESIRED OUTCOME without listing it, renaming a DESIRED OUTCOME while features keep the old name, editing or removing a feature's DESIRED OUTCOME list, or removing a feature.
doesNotFire: Every DESIRED OUTCOME in the plan is named in at least one feature's declared DESIRED OUTCOME list.
A feature lists DESIRED OUTCOMES beyond the minimum (only the DESIRED OUTCOME -> feature direction is checked).
The plan contains no DESIRED OUTCOMES.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role, covering both sides of the coverage enumeration: the covered kind (a DESIRED OUTCOME, which must be listed) and the covering kind (a feature, which carries the coverage list that names it). The check enumerates covered DESIRED OUTCOME artifacts and covering feature artifacts in the plan tree by these kinds.

The plan-artifact reference construct by which a covering feature artifact declares the plan artifacts it covers - the list in which every DESIRED OUTCOME must be named for the DESIRED OUTCOME -> feature coverage check.

neutralityNotes: The plan-graph terms DESIRED OUTCOME, feature, product capability and acceptance are ATDD methodology concepts (they appear as parametric values in the closed vocabulary, e.g. urn.desired-outcome) and are kept in the core; they name no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path. The concrete identification of both sides of the coverage enumeration in the plan - the covered DESIRED OUTCOME kind and the covering feature kind - comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds (Bun: desired outcome, feature, identifiable by file kind in the plan tree), and the feature's listing construct (Bun: the desired outcomes list) is carried by the map-key entry idiom.plan_syntax#coverage_list (plan-artifact reference construct; not URN grammar), so no new key is proposed. Validator, term and finding identifiers (test_all_desired_outcomes_in_at_least_one_feature, desired_outcome_feature_coverage) and the sidecar metadata.disposition pointer are Bun-only realization details; the per-rule disposition (documentation-only) is kept in core.verification per the notProfileKeys rule.
